This is my first visit to the Bell Tower, or Zhonglou (in Mandarin), is not just Xi'an's most iconic landmark; it is the geographical and spiritual heart of the ancient Ming Dynasty city. Standing proudly at the intersection of the four great avenues—connecting to the East, West, South, and North Gates of the City Wall—this majestic structure is the largest and best-preserved of its kind in all of China. From the site, it was built in 1384 and then famously relocated 1,000 meters east in 1582 (an incredible feat of ancient engineering!), the Bell Tower exemplifies the architectural prowess of the Ming Dynasty. It was originally used to signal the start of the day for the entire city, a tradition known as "morning bell and evening drum" (with the nearby Drum Tower). The Architecture and Engineering was the sophisticated brick-and-timber structure. The clever use of traditional Chinese Dougong (interlocking wooden brackets) showcases ingenuity, as the entire 36-meter-tall structure was assembled largely without nails. Note the triple-eaved roof and dark green glazed tiles that give it its regal appearance, just memorized me. The Bell Tower is absolutely breathtaking after sunset when it is completely bathed in golden illumination. The lighting accentuates its architectural details and creates a magical atmosphere, making it one of Xi'an’s best photo opportunities. My accommodation is just minutes walk to the the bell tower. For those whom need to commute in, the easiest way to reach the Bell Tower is by taking Metro Line 2 directly to Zhonglou Station. Use one of the underground exits that lead directly into the vast pedestrian tunnels surrounding the tower base, which is where the entrance is located.
Just an absolutely beautiful city sight at night. Even in the slow season large numbers of people gathering to share the brilliance. Many young women in period costumes osing for photo portraits.

At the intersection of the city's two main roads stands the 36-meter-high Bell Tower of Xi'an (西安鐘樓 - Xī'ān Zhōnglóu). The current bell tower, one of the grandest of its kind, was built in 1384 by order of the Hongwu Emperor and is the symbol of Xi'an. The tower originally stood on the grounds of the Yingxiang Temple (迎祥观) right in the middle of the city. In 1582, the bell tower was moved to its present location due to the shift in the city center due to expansion. Like other bell towers in China, the Xi'an bell tower was primarily used in ancient times to tell the time and announce news. Originally, the tower housed the gigantic Jingyun Bell, a bell from the Tang period. In 1953, this bell was moved to the Xi'an Stele Forest Museum, but in 1997, a replica was installed at the foot of the tower. The bell tower is beautifully illuminated, especially in the evening, and the square to its left is a popular place for a stroll.

The Bell Tower in Xi’an is a must-visit landmark, blending historical charm with modern accessibility. Conveniently accessible via the metro, it is located right in the heart of the city, making it easy to reach for locals and tourists alike. At night, the Bell Tower transforms into a mesmerizing sight, illuminated beautifully to highlight its intricate architecture. The glowing lights create a magical ambiance, perfect for capturing stunning photographs. For ladies, renting a Hanfu (traditional Chinese attire) adds an unforgettable cultural touch to the experience. Hanfu rentals typically cost around RMB 300, which usually includes makeup services. Renting a Hanfu for 24 hours allows plenty of time to explore the area and take photos. If you’re looking to capture professional-quality pictures, I recommend engaging an outside photographer rather than opting for the services provided by the Hanfu rental shops. The rates for external photographers are often more competitive and deliver better results. Overall, visiting the Bell Tower, especially in Hanfu, is an experience that beautifully combines history, culture, and modern aesthetics.

The entrance was a little confusing though. The underground signs say Exit 7, but actually the more accurate location should be the exit from metro Line 2 escalator (as one comes up from metro platform to the roundabout exits). The ticketing area is an automated self-service one but requires a local ID so I had to ask the staff for help and she used her ID to bypass the system for me. Later realised I could have just bought it on the CTrip app too, since the automated system uses Ctrip's system too. The prices are the same. Entrance fees are CNY30 per tower or CNY50 for both. The entrance to the Bell Tower is just beside the ticketing area. Followed the path through security checks and finally made it to the Bell Tower, which sits in the middle of the city in a roundabout. The Bell Tower was critical in the past to indicate time. Hence, there are a number of such similar towers in other cities such as Beijing. Today, it's more of a historic presence and showcase of ancient finess in architecture and construction. The architectural structure, the drawings within, the construction of such a huge bell.

The Bell Tower of Xi'an, standing majestically in the heart of the Zhonglou District, encapsulates the rich history and architectural splendor of Xi'an, China. This iconic structure, a testament to ancient Chinese ingenuity, is not merely a tower but a living chronicle of the city's past. As the sun sets, the Bell Tower transforms into a mesmerizing spectacle, bathed in radiant lights that highlight its intricate details. The night unveils a different dimension of its beauty, creating a breathtaking panorama that captivates both locals and tourists alike. Beyond its aesthetic allure, the Bell Tower carries the weight of historical significance. In bygone eras, it served a practical purpose—announcing the time at dawn to the bustling city. Its timekeeping function was not only utilitarian but also a cultural cornerstone, influencing the rhythm of daily life for the city's inhabitants. Ascending the tower, one is treated to panoramic views of Xi'an's urban landscape. The juxtaposition of ancient and modern structures tells a story of a city that has gracefully embraced the winds of change while safeguarding its historical roots. Visiting the Bell Tower is more than a tourist experience; it's a journey through time. Each step echoes with the footsteps of those who have come before, connecting the present with the city's storied past. Exploring its surroundings, one encounters lively markets, quaint shops, and a vibrant atmosphere that mirrors the dynamic spirit of Xi'an. My visits to the Bell Tower, often with friends enchanted by its allure, have been moments of contemplation and admiration. Its architectural grandeur and cultural resonance make it an indispensable gem in the heart of Xi'an. Whether under the golden hues of the sun or the ethereal glow of night, the Bell Tower remains a beacon, guiding travelers through Xi'an's historical narrative.

At the heart of Xi’an, where dynastic lines once drew the boundaries of ancient China, the Bell Tower stands—not as a ruin, but as a resonant witness. Built in 1384 during the Ming Dynasty, this towering structure once marked the city’s official center, its giant bell tolling across the walled capital at dawn. Today, surrounded by the rush of modern life and traffic loops spinning like clock hands around its base, the Bell Tower is a quiet assertion of continuity. Stone, timber, and glazed tiles merge in perfect symmetry, its triple-eaved roof glowing emerald and gold under dusk’s fading light. From above, it divides the city into compass points—four gates radiating from its core like arteries. Inside, the wooden staircases groan softly beneath your feet, and the echo of chimes—whether real or remembered—lingers in the rafters.

The Bell Tower of Xi'an (simplified Chinese: 西安钟楼; traditional Chinese: 西安鐘樓; pinyin: Xī'ān Zhōnglóu), built in 1384 during the early Ming Dynasty, is a symbol of the city of Xi'an and one of the grandest of its kind in China. The Bell Tower also contains several large bronze-cast bells from the Tang Dynasty. The tower base is square and it covers an area of 1,377 m2 (14,820 sq ft). The tower is a brick and timber structure and close to 40 m (130 ft) high. It is located in the center of Xi'an, at the intersection of the four streets of the east, west, south and north. It is the largest and most preserved one amongst the many bell towers left over from ancient China.

Xi'an Bell Tower is located in the city center. It was first built in the 17th year of Hongwu in the Ming Dynasty (AD 1384). The original site was at the intersection of Guangji Street, today's West Street. It was moved to the current location in the 10th year of Wanli in the Ming Dynasty (AD 1582) and became an axial building with an east-west hub and an echo between the north and south. In the past, there was a big bell hanging upstairs, which was used to announce alarms, hence the name Bell Tower.

西安鐘樓位於西安市中心，明城牆內東西南北四條大街的交匯處，是中國現存鐘樓中形制最大、保存最完整的一座。建於明太祖洪武十七年（1384年），初建於今廣濟街口，與鼓樓相對，明神宗萬曆十年（1582年）整體遷移於今址。 鐘樓建在方型基座之上，為磚木結構，重樓三層檐，四角攢頂的形式，總高36米，占地面積1377平方米。 鐘樓整體以磚木結構為主，構建於用青磚、白灰砌成的方形基座上。樓體為木質結構，深、廣各三間。 鐘樓的西北角懸掛的大鐘，已不再有報時的功用，但是逢年過節依然會被敲響，祈福平安。鐘樓一開始懸掛的並不是這口大鐘，而是鑄造於唐代的一口名為“景雲鐘”的大鐘。 遊覽路線 鐘樓-鼓樓-回民街-易俗歷史文化街區-開元商場觀景台(全程2.5小時，推薦晚上看夜景)

reviews.text: 西安鐘樓，已經有600多年歷史，建於明朝洪武年間建成。 鐘樓主要作用是通知西安人民一個預警報告。當有危險時候，有困難時候，鐘樓就會敲鐘，響起鐘聲，警醒附近百姓，通知。所謂一傳十，十傳百，百傳千。 西安鐘樓位於西安市中心，交通發達，四通八達，通往東南西北中心地帶。 今天沒有特別走上鐘樓，反而到了附近一個商場，開元廣場5樓平台離遠睇鐘樓一覽無遺景致十分之優美絕對是超值。

Campanario de Xi'an (Xī'ān Zhōnglóu), un hito histórico icónico y bien conservado construido en 1384 durante la dinastía Ming. Ubicado en el corazón del centro de Xi'an, esta gran estructura de madera y ladrillo sirvió originalmente para cronometrar la ciudad y ahora funciona como un museo popular, especialmente conocido por su impresionante iluminación nocturna que atrae a turistas y locales por igual.

La tour de la cloche se trouve en plein coeur du centre-ville de Xi'an, à l'intérieur des remparts. Située au milieu d'un rond-point, l'accès se fait par le sous-sol, via différents points d'accès avec, notamment, une sortie de métro. Le billet d'entrée coûte 30 CNY si vous ne visitez qu'une seule des deux tours ou alors 50 CNY si vous prenez le billet couplé avec la tour des tambours. La tour fut construite en 1384 et se trouve être unes des plus grandes de ce type en Chine. Elle abrite de nombreuses cloches, dont une des plus célèbres, la cloche jingyun pesant 6.5 tonnes et mesurant 2,46 m. Constituée de brique et de bois, elle mesure environ 40 m de haut. On peut accéder au balcon via des escaliers, il n'y a pas d'ascenseur. La visite est rapide, environ 30 min mais la vue vaut le coup d'oeil et le bâtiment en lui-même est joli. Il y a une petite partie musée intéressante.

Место мне понравилось. Мне вообще понравился Сиань. Тут хорошо сочетаются современные строения и традиционные формы пагод. Мы, иностранцы, не знаем истории, легенд и традиций этого места, поэтому нет смысла писать и оценивать историческое значение башни. Мы относимся не так, как местные, к достопримечательностям. Я был рано утром и, судя по количеству убираемого мусора, здесь тусовочное место и здесь до ночи гуляют люди. Мне понравились люди. Я немного пообщался и сфотографировался с китайской семьей, которая здесь гуляла. Так же пообщался немного и сфотографировался с группой молодых китайских девушек, которые приехали в Сиань из какого-то другого города. И у меня остались очень хорошие впечатления и воспоминания об это месте, как о культурном центре Сианя. В разных городах мира есть места, где люди просто гуляют. Мне кажется, что здесь как раз такое место по вечерам. Не экскурсионное место, а место, где люди гуляют и отдыхают. Поэтому, если у вас есть полчаса свободного времени в Сиане, я советую заехать сюда и посмотреть. Тем более станция метро находится рядом с этой башней и доехать очень легко.

Bell Tower of Xi'an – 西安钟楼 -Dieses ikonische Wahrzeichen der Stadt wirkt schon aus der Ferne majestätisch, doch erst wenn man unter seinen dreistöckigen Dächern mit dunkelgrünen glasierten Ziegeln und goldenen Details steht, erkennt man seine volle Schönheit. Besonders gut hat mir gefallen, dass sich der Turm direkt im geografischen Zentrum der Altstadt befindet, von wo aus die Hauptstraßen in alle Richtungen verlaufen – genau so, wie es Besucher und Reiseführer beschreiben. Im Inneren habe ich eine sehr angenehme Besichtigung genossen, einschließlich Repliken historischer Glocken und traditioneller Muster an den Balken, die unglaublich authentisch wirken. Der Ausblick vom oberen Stockwerk ist großartig – man hat das ganze geschäftige Zentrum von Xi’an wie auf der Handfläche, was auch viele Rezensionen bestätigen, die die Panoramaszenerie und die nächtliche Beleuchtung hervorheben. Ich schätze auch, dass der Zugang durch eine Unterführung sehr einfach ist, sodass man keine stark befahrene Kreuzung überqueren muss. Für mich definitiv ein Ort, der in jede Reiseroute in Xi’an gehört.

西安鐘樓建成於西元1384年(明朝洪武十七年)，位於中國陝西省西安市的市中心，城內東西南北四條大街的交匯處，是中國眾多鐘樓中形制最大、保存最完整的一座，鐘樓在古代主要用於報時，發布消息等；西安鐘樓就位在西安市的正中軸，可以從鐘樓看到西安現今東西南北向的發展。

La Torre del Campanile e la Torre del Tamburo della piazza sono le sue principali attrazioni, antichi simboli della Città Vecchia. Costruite durante la dinastia Ming, le torri un tempo erano utilizzate per tenere il tempo e oggi attirano turisti e gente del posto che si riuniscono nella piazza per ammirare la loro architettura. Nei dintorni belli folkloristici e un ricchissimo mercato locale che vende praticamente di tutto, dalle bancarelle di manifattura al più improbabile street food! Oltre a queste imponenti torri, ci sono una scelta di posti dove mangiare, fare acquisti e godersi alcune persone che guardano e musica dal vivo nella piazza. È il luogo perfetto per conoscere la storia di Xian e scattare alcune foto impressionanti. Siamo arrivati in piazza la mattina presto, abbiamo trovato un raduno di gente del posto, per lo più anziani, che svolgevano i loro esercizi mattutini. Visitata poi di notte e c'erano più giovani che facevano una passeggiata serale o semplicemente si godevano l'atmosfera, come noi.
鐘樓沒有太多東西可以看，但入場費卻收RMB30，實在有點貴。雖然叫做鐘樓，亦都有一個大鐘，但要留意這個是複製品。 位於有名的回民街附近，逛完可以找些東西吃。有時間可以看一下。 建議上網預先購票，沒有留意現場是否有售票的地方。

本座在西安鐘樓旁住了一週，第一天白天看了一會，想說一個不堪入目的門樓，有什麼值得誇讚的，華人世界到處都有這種建築，不以為意。 到了晚上在看，光華萬丈，車水馬龍繞行鐘樓，旅人爭相卡位拍照，直播主在一旁開元商場徹夜不停的在網上賣著旅遊活動，慢慢地讓我有了些感受。 接下來很多天都有經過，甚至晚上還得從地下街與地鐵站路過，此時的我終於明白，西安鐘樓這四個字，完全象徵性的代表了西安，不是大唐不夜城，也不是秦始皇兵馬俑，更不是華清宮長恨歌，更不是什麼陝歷博，而是這西安鐘樓，所有旅人踩到西安市，無不與鐘樓有關，從路線，行程，經濟，多個面向都是由此擴散，你說它普通，就是個樓，那表示你來西安旅遊還沒到位，而當你細細品味了這個不怎樣的景點或是路沖後，你會豁然開朗，原來這就是西安啊

鐘樓位於西安市中心位置， 亦是明古城牆的中央點。 地鐵站2號線「鐘樓」站9號出口。 買票處就在「鍾樓站」C出口。 （地鐵站內） 有幾部自助售票機， 電子支付即可。 門票¥30， 鐘樓+鼓樓¥50～ 65歲或以上免費入場（需換票入場） 鐘樓建於明朝， 已有近700年的歷史。 我認為是有觀賞性的景點。 鐘樓歷史悠久地 站立於道路中間的環形交叉路口上， 車輛會在城樓下穿梭往來。 登上鐘樓， 從馬路中心去欣賞市貌， 也是種風味～ 建議遊覽：鐘樓—》鼓樓—〉回民街帶～

Felülete kék tégla, alapja kétszintes fa szerkezetű. Tetejét sötétzöld mázas tetőcserepek borítják, a belső teret aranyfestmények díszítik. Kína legjobban megőrzött fa épülete.

시안의 종루(钟楼.Bell Tower of XI'an,7W5W+QRJ, Bei Lin Qu, Xi'An, Shaanxi, China)는 장안성 남문에서 북쪽으로600m 떨어져 있으며 고루와는 260m 거리로 한눈에 보인다. 종루는 시안의 동서남북을 연결하는 중심지에 위치하며 시안 여행의 시작점으로1384년 명나라 태조 홍무제에 의해 지어진 40m 높이의 정사각형 목조 건축물로 중국의 종루중 가장 크며 종루에는 당나라 시대에 만들어진 대형 청동 주조 종이 여러개가 있다.날이 밝았음을 알려주기 위해 종을 쳐서 시계탑 역할을 하였는데 아침 종으로도 불린다.야경이 아름답기로 소문난 시안의 랜드마크이다. 종루는 회전교차로 안에 섬처럼 고립되어 있어 지하도를 통해서 가야한다.오후19시 부터 종루의 야경 일루미네이션이 시작되며 입장료는 35원이지만 고루와의 통합권 입장료는 50원입니다.

西安钟楼 钟楼和鼓楼 联票(钟楼和鼓楼)50人民币 单买各30 建于明太祖洪武十七年(1384年)，初建于今广济街口，与鼓楼相对，明神宗万历十年(1582年)整体迁移于今址。 西安钟鼓楼是钟楼和鼓楼的合称，正所谓“晨钟暮鼓”，但说的并不是早晨敲钟、晚上敲鼓。而是早晨先敲钟后敲鼓，晚上先敲鼓后敲钟。 这两座城楼修建于大明王朝。当年，朱元璋曾想把国都迁到西安，特派太子朱标前去考察，并按帝都标准修建了钟鼓楼。太子朱标圆满完成了父亲交代的任务，回到南京献出了陕西地图，但却随即病倒，不久便一命呜呼。白发人送黑发人，在晚年失去自己最挚爱的儿子，朱元璋深受打击，从此西安成为朱元璋心中的一个伤痕，迁都的事就此不提。
